# opencode-gitlab-titler

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) server plugin that names a session after the GitLab merge request or issue in your first message, so you can find the session later by project, number or title.

| First message | Session title |
|---|---|
| mentions "review" and links an MR | `Reviewing (gitlab-org/gitlab\|!123) MR title` |
| links an issue (with or without "review", unless it also reviews an MR) | `(gitlab-org/gitlab\|#45) Issue title` |
| no "review", links an MR you wrote | `(gitlab-org/gitlab\|!123) MR title` |
| anything else | OpenCode's own title, guided to the same format when the message names an item |

The MR or issue is fetched with one `glab api` request. It runs inside OpenCode's `title` hook, which fires once per session while the title is generated, so the name is set before any work starts and nothing renames it later.

## Rules

1. The first MR link and the first issue link in the message are the ones used. Other links are ignored.
2. "review" means the word `review`, `reviews`, `reviewed` or `reviewing`, in any case. `preview` and `code_review` do not count.
3. Review and an MR link: always a review title, whoever wrote the MR. This wins even when the message also links an issue.
4. Any issue link otherwise: an issue title, even when the message says "review". An issue next to "review" and no MR means you are starting work on it, not reviewing it. The issue also wins over an MR that is not being reviewed.
5. No review, no issue, and an MR link: the MR is named only when its author is you. Someone else's MR gets the default title, with no guidance.
6. Anything else, including review with no link: the default title, with guidance (below).
7. If GitLab cannot be reached, or `glab` fails, the plugin logs `[gitlab-titler] no GitLab title: <reason>` and falls back to the default title, with guidance. A GitLab problem never blocks a session.

A link is `https://<host>/<project path>/-/merge_requests/<n>`, `/-/issues/<n>` or `/-/work_items/<n>`. Work items are looked up as issues.

## Guided titles

Not every session starts with a link. "Continue work on issue 45" or "pick up gitlab-org/gitlab!123" names an item but gives the plugin nothing to fetch. In those cases, and whenever the link lookup fails, the plugin adds a short instruction to OpenCode's own title request. It asks the title model to use the same shapes when one item is clearly identified and clearly being worked on:

- `Reviewing (<project>|!<iid>) <description>` for a merge request being reviewed
- `(<project>|#<iid>) <description>` for an issue, even when the message says review
- `(<project>|!<iid>) <description>` for a merge request being worked on

The model cannot fetch the real title, so it writes the description from your message. It is told to take the project and number from the message, to use `defaultProject` for a number with no project, never to invent either, and otherwise to write a normal title. Set `guideTitle` to `false` to turn this off. A title the plugin builds from GitLab never uses the model, so it is never guided.

## The `/gitlab-titler` command

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/gitlab-titler enable` | Turn the plugin on for the current project. |
| `/gitlab-titler disable` | Turn it off for the current project. New sessions get OpenCode's own title, with no guidance. |
| `/gitlab-titler retitle` | Name the current session again, from the whole conversation. |
| `/gitlab-titler` | Open a dialog with the same choices. So does any text it does not understand, after a warning. |

The dialog shows whether the plugin is on, offers to flip it, and offers "Retitle this session". Retitle is greyed out on the home screen. The setting is stored per project, not per session, and survives restarts. The plugin is on until you turn it off. Retitle works whether the plugin is on or off.

The command is also in the command palette as "GitLab titler".

### Retitle

The automatic title only ever sees the first message. Retitle looks at the whole session, so it can follow work that has moved on: an issue you picked up later, or an MR you opened.

1. It reads the session's messages: everything you typed, the assistant's prose and any compaction summary. Tool calls, reasoning and shell output are left out. A long session keeps its start and its most recent messages, up to about 12,000 characters, and says how many it dropped.
2. It looks up the real title of the first MR and the first issue you linked anywhere in the session, so the title model can reuse them instead of guessing.
3. It sends the transcript, those titles and the same format instructions as the guided title to the title model, and asks for one line.
4. It cleans the answer (quotes, a `Title:` label, a second line), cuts it to `maxTitleLength` and renames the session.

If the model returns nothing usable, the session has no messages, or the model call fails, the title is left alone and you see a toast with the reason.

Which model: the model set for the `title` agent in your OpenCode config, if there is one.

```jsonc
{
  "agents": {
    "title": { "model": "gitlab/duo-chat-haiku-5-5" }
  }
}
```

Without that, the model OpenCode itself last used to title a session, which is its own small-model choice. If no title has been generated since the plugin was installed, OpenCode's default model is used. The plugin reads the config on every retitle, so changing `agents.title.model` needs no restart.

## `/review-swarm`

If you use a `/review-swarm` command that expands to a prompt with a `**MR to review:** <iid>` line and no link, set `defaultProject` (and `hosts`, if the project is not on gitlab.com). That line is the one place a bare IID is understood. It is read as an MR in `defaultProject` on the first entry in `hosts`.

## Install

Requirements:

- OpenCode 2.0.9 or newer.
- [`glab`](https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli) installed and signed in to every host you use: `glab auth login` (add `--hostname <host>` for a self-managed instance). Check with `glab api user`.

Add the package to `plugins` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. OpenCode installs it and its dependencies. One entry loads the server part (title hook, on/off setting, retitle) and the terminal part (`/gitlab-titler`):

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["opencode-gitlab-titler"]
}
```

Pin a version with `"opencode-gitlab-titler@0.1.0"`. To set options, use the object form:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "opencode-gitlab-titler",
      "options": {
        "hosts": ["gitlab.com", "gitlab.example.com"],
        "maxTitleLength": 200
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Run `/reload` or start a new session. To check it loaded, type `/gitlab-titler`, or start a new session with an MR link as the first message.

### From a local checkout

Run `bun install` once in the checkout, then point `package` at the directory:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [{ "package": "file:///path/to/opencode-gitlab-titler" }]
}
```

### Uninstall

Remove the entry from `plugins`. The per-project on/off setting stays in OpenCode's plugin storage and does nothing without the plugin.

## Options

All options are optional. A value of the wrong type is ignored and the default is used, so a typo cannot stop the plugin from loading.

| Option | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `maxTitleLength` | `100` | Longest the MR or issue title can be before it is cut with `…`. At least 10. The project and number are never cut. |
| `currentUser` | looked up with `glab api user` | GitLab username that counts as you for MRs without "review". Set it to skip the lookup. |
| `defaultProject` | `gitlab-org/gitlab` | Project for a bare IID from `/review-swarm`. |
| `hosts` | `["gitlab.com"]` | Hosts a link may point at. Links to any other host are ignored and never fetched. |
| `timeoutSeconds` | `15` | How long one `glab` call may take. |
| `guideTitle` | `true` | Add the title format to OpenCode's title request when the plugin cannot build a title from a link. |

`glab` is found through `$GLAB_PATH`, then `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` and `~/.local/bin`, then `PATH`, because the OpenCode server may not have Homebrew on its `PATH`.

## Safety

- Read-only: `glab api` is only ever given a path, so it can only send GET. The tests check this.
- `glab` is started with an argument array and no shell, so nothing in a message can be run as a command.
- Links to hosts outside `hosts` are never fetched.
- The plugin never reads or stores a token. `glab` holds the credentials.
- Retitle sends a trimmed copy of your conversation to the title model. That is the same model that already sees your first message, and it is the only place the plugin sends more than that.

## Troubleshooting

The plugin warns with lines starting `[gitlab-titler]`. They are written by the OpenCode server process, so look in the server log (`~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`) or its output. The messages below follow that prefix.

| Symptom | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `no GitLab title: spawn glab ENOENT` | `glab` is not installed or not in a place the server looks. Install it, or set `GLAB_PATH` in the environment OpenCode starts from. |
| `no GitLab title:` with an authentication error | `glab` is not signed in to that host. Run `glab auth login --hostname <host>`. |
| A self-managed link is ignored | The host is not in `hosts`. Add it. |
| The session gets OpenCode's own title | The plugin is off for this project (`/gitlab-titler enable`), the link is not an MR or issue link, or the MR is someone else's and the message does not say "review". |
| `/gitlab-titler` is missing | The terminal part did not load. Run `/reload` and check the entry in `opencode.jsonc` and your OpenCode version. |

## Development

OpenCode reloads a plugin every time one of its files is saved, in every open session. Do not edit this plugin while it is listed in your OpenCode config. Remove it from `plugins`, edit and test, then add it back.

```sh
bun install
bun test
bun run typecheck
```

The tests never touch the network or a running OpenCode.

| File | Does |
|---|---|
| `src/refs.ts` | Finds links in the message and decides which one names the session. |
| `src/title.ts` | Builds the title string and cuts it to length. |
| `src/gitlab.ts` | Talks to `glab`. The only file with side effects, and only `glabRunner`. |
| `src/resolve.ts` | Turns a message into a title, "leave it alone", or "guide the model". |
| `src/guidance.ts` | The format instructions added to the title request. |
| `src/hook.ts` | The `title` hook body: on/off, then resolve, then set the title or add guidance. |
| `src/state.ts` | The per-project on/off setting and the remembered title model. |
| `src/transcript.ts`, `src/retitle.ts` | Retitle: render the session, build the prompt, call the model, rename. |
| `src/service.ts`, `src/rpc.ts` | The server side of `/gitlab-titler` and its RPC contract. |
| `src/command.ts`, `src/tui.ts` | The slash command: logic, and the terminal wiring. |
| `src/index.ts` | The server part: wires everything to OpenCode. |

### Testing against a real server

Unit tests cover the logic. To exercise the title hook, the RPC and retitle against a real OpenCode, use a plugin lab (the author's is `opencode-plugin-lab`, not part of this package). It starts a private server with its own database and a mock model, so it cannot reach your sessions or the shared service. The checks that matter: titles for an issue link, a review, a review with only an issue link and no link at all; the guidance reaching the title request; `setEnabled` switching the hook off and on; `retitle` renaming a session and failing cleanly on an empty one; one `loading plugin` line per location; no errors in the server log.

The terminal part (`src/tui.ts`) needs a real TUI. Its logic is in `src/command.ts` and is unit tested; only the wiring to the dialog and toast is not.

## Publishing

```sh
bun install
npm version <patch|minor|major>
npm publish   # runs typecheck and tests first (prepublishOnly)
```

`npm pack --dry-run` should list only `src/`, `README.md`, `LICENSE` and `package.json`. The package ships TypeScript source, which OpenCode runs directly, so there is no build step.
